title: Rav Zutra
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: “In the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,” Berakhot 43a: he said, “It is better for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace than to humiliate his fellow in public.” So Seder HaDorot cites it, and the author of Maskil LeEitan raised an outcry against him that it is not found there and argued there needlessly, in Hyman’s judgment, for that is the reading of Ein Yaakov there. Hyman considers it very likely that he is Rabbi Zutra the Babylonian Tanna.

notes.text: Maskil LeEitan is a work title, not a place or a rabbi named LeEitan. The supplied עלי is not made into an assertion that the earlier author disputed Hyman personally. The supplied Berakhot 43a remains beside saved Davidson 43b, whose alternative chains differ from Hyman’s Ein Yaakov report. Rabbi Zutra in the conjectural closing identification is not harmonized to the heading Rav Zutra.
